prerequisites: Solid knowledge of the notions provided by the course of Signal Theory: Fourier theory of periodic and aperiodic deterministic signals, random variables, stochastic processes and their spectral analysis.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the basic principles of telecommunications, the characteristics of the signals used and their propagation modes.
Knowledge and understanding of the different analog and digital signal modulation and demodulation systems.
Knowledge and understanding of the disturbances affecting the received signals and their statistical characterization.
Ability to characterize, analyze and quantify signal disturbances and their effects.
Ability to comparatively and critically analyze the different transmission and reception, modulation and demodulation schemes.
Ability to make autonomous choices regarding the design of an analog or digital telecommunications system.
Ability to logically present demonstrations related to the characterization of random signals and disturbances.
Ability to logically present technical demonstrations on the characteristics of specific telecommunications systems.
Ability to autonomously carry out the complete characterization of a telecommunications system.

syllabus_topics: Transmission via modulation of analog and digital signals.
Efficiency of modulation/demodulation schemes against noise.

Introduction to communication systems: information and disturbance, information sources, architecture of a communication system, wireless and wired communication systems, frequency allocation, notes on signal propagation mode, with particular reference to wireless systems.
Disturbances in communication systems: band-filtered white noise, thermal noise, noise figure, equivalent noise temperature, noise figure of cascaded systems.

Analog modulations. Classic AM modulation, AM-DSB modulation, AM-SSB modulation, angular modulations (PM and FM). Modulators and demodulators, noise performance, threshold effect. Signal multiplexing: FDM and TDM. Superheterodyne and homodyne receivers.

Numerical modulations. Baseband pulse modulations: "flat top" and "natural gating" PAM, PDM and PPM, quantized pulse modulations, PCM, differential PCM, line codes: unipolar and bipolar NRZ and RZ. Gray coding. Binary numerical modulations: OOK, BPSK, FSK and CPFSK. Transmission band. Relationship between total signal-to-noise ratio, signal-to-noise ratio per bit and spectral efficiency. Multilevel modulations: M-PAM, M-PSK (QPSK and OQPSK), QAM. Transmission band and spectral efficiency. Error probability in numerical modulations: decision regions and maximum likelihood receiver. Optimal receiver schemes. Error bound.
assessment_rules: The oral exam verifies knowledge and understanding of basic principles, modulation/demodulation systems, and disturbances, as well as the ability to apply this knowledge through exercises. The assessment ranges from 'Insufficient' for severe conceptual errors to '29-30 e Lode' for complete, in-depth knowledge and critical thinking. 'Lode' (cum laude) is awarded for excellent and original performance.
